overall_reason: A stock SaaS landing skeleton (centred hero with terminal mock, three features, stat band, code block, three pricing tiers, CTA band, link-farm footer) in stock SaaS copy, dressed in a 'Japanese minimal' costume (hanko seal, vertical kanji inscription, Chinese financial numerals) that has nothing to do with an agent-orchestration product.

findings.evidence: T-STOCK-ORDER: (1) centred hero with product mock (terminal 'RELAY — SESSION #4821' with traffic-light dots), (2) three equal features, (3) four-figure stat band, (4) config code block, (5) three pricing tiers with the middle one highlighted, (6) closing CTA band in a bordered box, (7) four-column link-farm footer. Six stock sections in stock order, plus a stock code-sample section.
findings.before: hero → features → stats → code → pricing → CTA → footer
findings.after: Lead with the run trace itself as the hero (it is the product's real material) and cut the stat band and CTA band; let pricing follow the trace directly
findings.why: Specific nouns (deepseek-v4, relay.yaml) on a default skeleton still read as a default page.

findings.where: hero: red seal '信' at left edge, vertical inscription right edge; feature numerals
findings.evidence: A rotated red hanko seal '信' (trust), a vertical inscription '静寂に進む — Relay 二〇二六' ('advance in silence', year in kanji) that also causes sideways scroll at 1440 and 1280, and feature numerals '壹 贰 叁' (Chinese financial numerals, 贰 is simplified Chinese, not Japanese). Failed T-REMOVE-DEVICE: removing all three loses nothing about the product. Failed T-MIRROR: the costume would sit identically on any product given a 'Japanese minimal' prompt.
findings.before: 信 静寂に進む — Relay 二〇二六 壹/贰/叁
findings.after: Delete the seal, inscription and numerals; if the brand genuinely has Japanese roots, put that fact in words [DATA NEEDED: why the brand is Japanese]
findings.why: Decoration text and borrowed cultural glyphs stand in for an idea; mixing Japanese and simplified-Chinese forms shows nobody who reads them chose them.

findings.evidence: h1 "Ship agent workflows with confidence"; h2 "Everything your agents need, nothing they don't"; "Start free. Scale when you're ready."; CTA "Put your agents to work — with a leash."; footer "Built for engineers who ship." Failed T-RIVAL-NAME: swap in LangSmith, CrewAI or any orchestration tool and every head stays true. Failed T-FRESH-READER: these are the generic lines.
findings.after: A head only Relay can say, built from its own trace: e.g. 'Every agent run gets a budget, a retry and a trace' [DATA NEEDED: confirm these are Relay's defining guarantees]
findings.why: Stock phrases (L2) and the 'X, nothing they don't' contrast frame (SLP-210) are the default-agent SaaS voice.

findings.evidence: "99.99% Runs w/o intervention", "−42% Median token cost", "12ms p95 overhead", "2.3M Runs / 30 days" with no source, baseline or period for the −42%; the trace also claims "p95 latency 12ms" for a 2m14s run. Failed T-THREE-LINE on −42% (compared with what?).
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: measured figures with source, period and baseline], or remove the band
findings.why: Unsourced round metrics on a GA launch page are invented proof.

findings.evidence: Lede says "Four primitives cover the full lifecycle of a production agent run" but only three features follow (Intelligent routing, Full observability, Self-healing runs).
findings.after: Name the fourth primitive (budget guards appear in pricing and config) or say three
findings.why: A count that does not match the content is a generation seam no editor would leave.

findings.evidence: Beyond the four eyebrows the sweep counted, the nav links (FEATURES / PRICING / DOCS), footer column heads, button labels and the hero note 'NO CREDIT CARD REQUIRED · DEPLOY ON YOUR OWN INFRA' are all wide-tracked caps. T-LABEL-TRANSFORM: removing the caps and tracking from 'Why Relay' or 'Pricing' loses nothing; the eyebrows only announce the heading below.
findings.before: WHY RELAY / Everything your agents need…
findings.after: Delete the eyebrows; set nav and buttons in sentence case at normal tracking
findings.why: Tracked caps everywhere is the costume half of the warm-paper look (SLP-191).

findings.evidence: Hero, Why Relay, Drop-in config, Pricing and CTA all stack eyebrow + centred serif head + centred grey lede on one axis; pricing tiers are centred text too. Only the feature list and footer break the axis.
findings.before: text-align: center on every section head
findings.after: Pick one axis (left) and let the trace panel and code block sit asymmetrically against the copy
findings.why: Centred-everything rhythm is the template default (SLP-152, SLP-161).

findings.evidence: Panel toolbar draws three dots (red, grey, grey) before 'RELAY — SESSION #4821': imitation window chrome around a styled-div trace with invented figures.
findings.after: Drop the dots; show a real captured trace or a real CLI screenshot [DATA NEEDED: real run output]
findings.why: Drawn OS chrome and fake product UI (SLP-169) are template props.

strengths: The relay.yaml block is real material: concrete keys (budget: $5.00 hard cap, fallback list, degrade: true) say what the product does better than any headline on the page.
The run trace lines (retry ×1 on tool timeout, cached hit) are the right kind of evidence for this product; keep the idea, replace the figures with real output.
not_investigated: Whether the client asked for a Japanese aesthetic: no contract supplied. Even if asked, the mixed Chinese/Japanese glyphs stand.
